transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess what brings me in is these awful doubts I keep having, like I’ve missed something important. A number on the mortgage payment, or some clause in a client proof—I'm a graphic designer, so there are always tiny things to catch—or even whether a door is properly latched.

And the thing is, I know I checked it. Or I think I know. But then the thought just barges back in, like, “What if this is the mistake that costs you everything?” It sounds dramatic when I say it out loud… but it feels very real in the moment.
Do you find yourself doing anything over and over to try to get rid of these doubts?

Yes… I do. I’ll reopen the same files again and again, reread emails I already read, check the online payment confirmation more than once. With invoices especially, I’ll kind of say the numbers silently in my head until they feel… I don’t know, “settled,” I guess.

And then what should be, like, a quick logo revision or sending off one simple invoice turns into this whole ordeal. Hours can disappear, and I can’t even bill for that time, which is ridiculous because I’m just sitting there checking, not really designing.
Do you find yourself performing any physical actions repeatedly, like touching or tapping, as part of trying to get rid of these doubts?

Not really tapping, I don’t think… not in a noticeable way. It’s more on the computer, if that counts as physical—I keep reopening the same file, rereading the same email, checking the payment confirmation again.

Sometimes I’ll just sit there with the invoice numbers and say them silently in my head until they feel right, or “settled.” Which is embarrassing because it’s not like I’m doing more work. I mean, I’ll plan to send one invoice and then suddenly it’s been an hour or two, and I haven’t even done anything I can bill for.
Do you feel anxious when these doubts occur?

Yes—very anxious. It’s not just a little “oh, did I forget?” feeling. It comes in like this awful doubt, like maybe I missed a number on the mortgage payment or a clause in a client proof, or something simple like whether the door actually latched.

And even if I know I checked it, or I’m almost sure I did, my mind just circles back with, “What if this is the mistake that costs you everything?” Which is… I mean, I know that sounds extreme. My husband would probably say I make everything into a catastrophe—well, not everything, but you know. In the moment it really does feel like something terrible could happen if I don’t catch it.
Do these doubts and fears that you're experiencing seem to be focused on specific things, like the examples you've mentioned, or do you feel anxious about a wide range of things in general?

It’s more specific, I think. I mean, I can worry generally too—who doesn’t—but the really awful ones are these doubts that I’ve missed something important. Like a number on the mortgage payment, or some clause in a client proof, or whether the door actually latched.

And then even if I know I checked it, it comes barging back in like, “But what if this is the mistake that costs you everything?” Which sounds dramatic when I say it out loud. My sister is like that with travel plans, actually—she’ll print everything twice, which I used to tease her about—but this feels different. Mine sort of hooks onto these specific things where there could be a mistake and then I can’t let it go.
Do you feel like checking these things repeatedly is actually preventing something bad from happening?

I guess in the moment it feels like it is, yes. Like if I reopen the file one more time or reread the email again, then I’ll catch the thing before it turns into a disaster.

But then it gets ridiculous, because I’m checking the online payment confirmation, and then checking it again, and sometimes I’m just saying the figures silently in my head until they feel… settled, I guess. And it’s not even productive. A simple invoice or a logo revision can turn into hours I can’t bill for, and then I’m behind on everything else.
Do you feel less anxious after you've checked something repeatedly?

A little, yes—but it’s not a clean kind of relief. It’s more like I reopen the file, or reread the email, or check the online payment confirmation, and for maybe a minute I feel like, okay, that’s settled.

But then I’ll think, wait, did I really look at the right number? And I’ll go back again. Sometimes I’m just saying the figures silently in my head until they feel… I don’t know, firm enough. It’s silly, because a simple invoice or a logo revision can eat up hours, and I can’t even bill for that time. Then I’m behind, which is its own mess.
Do you think that if you didn't check these things repeatedly, something bad would actually happen?

I don’t know if I’d say I believe it completely, like logically. But in the moment, it feels like if I don’t check, I’m leaving the door open for something to go wrong.

So I’ll reopen the file, reread the email, check the online payment confirmation… and sometimes I’m just repeating the figures in my head until they feel settled. Which is embarrassing, because it can take a simple invoice or a logo revision and turn it into hours I can’t bill for. And then I’m annoyed at myself, but also afraid to stop.
When you repeat these checks, are you trying to prevent something specific from happening, like a financial loss or a mistake, or are you just trying to feel less anxious in general?

It’s more about preventing a mistake, I think… though it turns into just trying to make the anxious feeling stop. Like I’ll reopen the file, reread the email, check the online payment confirmation, and then sometimes I’m just saying the figures silently in my head until they feel “settled.”

And the stupid thing is, it’ll be something small—well, not small, but normal—like an invoice or a logo revision, and suddenly I’ve spent hours on it. Hours I can’t even bill for. Then I’m behind, and I start thinking I should’ve just trusted myself, but I don’t.
Are you checking these things repeatedly more to reduce your anxiety or to actually prevent a mistake from happening?

I think it starts as preventing a mistake. Like, if I don’t reopen the file or reread the email, I’ll miss something, or the payment confirmation won’t be right somehow.

But then it stops being practical. I’ll check it, and then check it again, and sometimes I’m just repeating the figures in my head until they feel… settled, I guess. It’s like the checking becomes the thing I have to finish before I can move on. And meanwhile a simple invoice or a logo revision has taken hours I can’t bill for, which is ridiculous.
Do you feel like there's a 'right' or 'exact' way to perform these checks, like a certain number of times or in a specific order?

Not a number exactly, no… it’s more like there’s a way it has to feel before I can stop. I’ll reopen the file, then reread the email, then check the payment confirmation, and if something still feels off I go back again.

Sometimes I’m just sitting there saying the figures silently in my head until they feel settled, which sounds silly when I say it out loud. And then I’ll look up and realize this was supposed to be a simple invoice or a logo revision, and I’ve spent hours on it—hours I can’t bill for.
Do you feel like there's a specific way you need to perform your daily tasks, like a certain order or pattern, for them to feel complete?

Yes, sort of. Not like a formal pattern exactly, but there’s this sequence I fall into. I’ll reopen the file, then reread the email, then check the online payment confirmation… and sometimes I’m just repeating the figures silently in my head until they feel settled.

It’s funny, because with design work there are already so many little details—colors, spacing, whether the logo looks balanced—and I can lose time there anyway. But this is different. A simple invoice or a logo revision can turn into hours, and I can’t bill for that time. I’ll think I’m just doing one more check, and then somehow I’m still there.
Do you feel like things need to be symmetrical or just right for you to consider them complete?

Not so much symmetrical, no. I mean, in design I care about balance, obviously—like if a logo is a little off it can drive anyone mad, and clients can be very particular about that too.

But with this, it’s more that things don’t feel complete until I’ve done the checking in the right way, or until it feels settled. I’ll reopen the file, reread the email, check the online payment confirmation, and sometimes I’m just sitting there saying the figures in my head quietly. Then a simple invoice or a small logo revision turns into hours I can’t bill for.
Do you feel like you're doing these checks to maintain control over your work or to avoid making a mistake?

I think it’s more to avoid making a mistake, though it probably is about control too, in a way. I mean, with design work, one tiny wrong amount on an invoice or one missed note in an email can make me look careless, and I hate that feeling.

So I’ll reopen the file, reread the email, check the online payment confirmation… and then sometimes I’m just saying the numbers silently in my head until they feel settled. And then, you know, I remember I was only supposed to be doing a quick invoice or a little logo revision, and suddenly it’s taken hours I can’t bill for.
Do you feel like your checks need to be perfect, or that if you don't do them a certain way, they won't be effective?

Yes… I think it does have to feel like I’ve done it the “right” way, otherwise I don’t trust it. Like I’ll reopen the file again, then reread the email, then go back to the online payment confirmation, and if I skip one of those or do it too quickly, it’s like it doesn’t count.

And sometimes I’ll just keep repeating the figures silently in my head until they feel settled, which sounds silly when I say it out loud. It can be something tiny, like an invoice or a logo revision, and suddenly I’ve spent hours on it that I can’t even bill for.
Do you think that if you didn't check things exactly as you do, the outcome would be unacceptable, even if it's not necessarily wrong?

Yes, I think that’s a good way to put it. It’s not always that I know something is wrong, it’s more that if I haven’t checked it in my exact little sequence, it feels… unfinished, or unsafe somehow.

Like I’ll reopen the file, then reread the email, then check the online payment confirmation, and sometimes I’m sitting there silently repeating the figures in my head until they feel settled. Which is ridiculous, because it might just be a simple invoice or a tiny logo revision—something I used to knock out quickly. And then I look up and I’ve lost hours I can’t bill for.

It’s not even that the outcome would definitely be wrong. It’s that I can’t let it go unless I’ve done the checking the way my brain says counts.
Do you think the reason you keep checking is mostly because you're afraid of making a mistake, or is it because you feel like you need to be in control of every detail?

Mostly it’s the fear of a mistake, I think… though control is tangled up in it. What brings me in is these awful doubts that I’ve missed something important, like a number on the mortgage payment, or a clause in a client proof, or even a door not being latched properly.

And I know that sounds like a random list, but that’s how it feels in my head—it jumps around. I can check something, and then the thought barges back in like, what if this is the mistake that costs you everything? And then I can’t just move on, because it feels too risky.
Is your need to check things repeatedly more about avoiding a mistake or feeling in control of the situation?

I think it’s more about avoiding a mistake, honestly. Or avoiding that feeling that I’ve missed something important.

It’ll be something like a number on the mortgage payment, or a clause in a client proof, or whether a door actually latched… and I know those aren’t all the same kind of thing, but they sort of feel the same in my head. Even after I check, the thought comes back in, like, what if this is the one thing you missed, the one that ruins everything?

I mean, I do like to feel in control, sure, but the panic is really about the possibility that I’ve overlooked something and won’t catch it in time.
Is the feeling that drives you to check things repeatedly more about the fear of something going wrong or the need to feel in control of the details?

It’s more the fear of something going wrong, I think. Like I can’t shake these doubts that I’ve missed something important.

It might be a number on the mortgage payment, or some clause in a client proof, or even whether a door actually latched. And even when I know I checked it—like, logically I know I looked—the thought comes barging back in: what if this is the mistake that costs you everything?

I suppose control is part of it, but it’s really that awful “what if” that keeps dragging me back.
Do you feel like the numbers or details you're checking need to be in a specific order or sequence for you to feel settled?

Not exactly in a sequence, no… it’s more that they don’t feel “settled” unless I go back over them enough times.

Like with an invoice or a logo revision, I’ll reopen the file, reread the email, check the online payment confirmation again. Sometimes I’ll say the figures silently in my head, almost like I’m trying to make them land properly. Which sounds strange when I say it out loud.

And then, you know, something that should take a few minutes turns into hours I can’t even bill for, because I’m just circling around the same details.
